answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to stake a refundable deposit tied to a verified work history before it can trade. A newcomer must complete small, checkable tasks over time, building a reputation that cannot be bought in bulk. A hollow identity with no history earns no trust, while creating thousands of fake accounts means funding thousands of deposits and doing real work for each, like pushing a dune grain by grain against a zephyr. The cost grows with every fake, so mass forgery becomes uneconomical while honest agents pay only once.
